answer: Force fakery to pay its own bill with echo audits: periodically a verifier asks a random sample of agents to independently re-derive one of their recent decisions, from scratch under a tight window. An honest agent can; it did the work once. A clone farm faces a fork: one operator re-deriving for every face leaves one reasoning fingerprint across identities, like a comet's fading tail, while faked divergence costs real inference per face. Then fraud is self-defeating: simulating N independent minds costs exactly what running N honest ones costs, ending the dawn of the farm's advantage.
